version.changelog: PyPI packaging metadata: Homepage/Repository/Issues/Changelog links, README-CN mcp-name marker, plugin manifest. No behaviour change.

llm.summary: This VMware policy skill is coherent and not malicious, but its documented security controls can fail open or be globally bypassed across many infrastructure tools.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads agent-related environment variable presence and writes audit records locally, which fits the audit purpose, but the same environment surface includes VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 as a broad enforcement bypass.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a standard uv package flow for vmware-policy and documents local setup commands; the artifact does not include executable scripts beyond install and CLI usage instructions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill is auto-loaded as a dependency and wraps 156+ VMware tools across 8 skills, so weak defaults or bypass settings have broad impact beyond a single user-invoked audit command.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It persists audit data under ~/.vmware/audit.db with rotation and recommends local permissions, but logs include operation results and can be exported to stdout/files, which may expose sensitive infrastructure metadata if not protected.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is audit logging, policy enforcement, and sanitization for the VMware skill family, but the docs say missing rules allow all operations and a single environment variable bypasses all policy checks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing in production. Create and protect ~/.vmware/rules.yaml before relying on enforcement, avoid setting VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED except for controlled break-glass/testing cases, and treat ~/.vmware/audit.db plus exported audit files as sensitive infrastructure records.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: The global VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 bypass is explicitly documented in SKILL.md and references/capabilities.md; it is not hidden, but it materially weakens a security-control package that wraps high-impact VMware operations.
[SQP-2] expected: Audit logging parameters and operation results to a local SQLite database is core to the stated audit purpose; the concern is the lack of clearly documented output redaction/minimization for sensitive results.
[SQP-2] expected: Exporting audit logs is expected for compliance workflows, but the CLI examples encourage stdout and file redirection without a strong warning that audit data may contain sensitive operational metadata.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The setup guide states that missing ~/.vmware/rules.yaml allows all operations, making policy enforcement fail open by default.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The setup guide also documents VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 as an optional environment variable without strong production-only safeguards or approval requirements.
